Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: After the talks, _____ retired to Thailand and Ah Hai replaced him as acting Secretary-General in Malaya
Baling Talks.fact: The main participants were Tunku Abdul Rahman (representing the Government of the Federation of Malaya), David Marshall (representing the Crown Colony of Singapore), and Chin Peng (representing the Malayan Communist Party). After the talks, Chin Peng retired to Thailand and Ah Hai replaced him as acting Secretary-General in Malaya.

Baling Talks.fact: There was an insurrection, and guerrilla war was fought between government forces and the Malayan National Liberation Army (MNLA) during the period.

Baling Talks.fact: The Government of Singapore issued an identical offer at the same time.

Baling Talks.question: However, few _____ surrendered to the authorities
Baling Talks.fact: On 8 September 1955, the Government of the Federation of Malaya issued a declaration of amnesty to the Communists. However, few Communists surrendered to the authorities.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: Realizing that his struggles had not come to any fruition, Chin Peng proposed a referendum to the ruling British government alongside many Malayan officials in _____
Baling Talks.fact: Realizing that his struggles had not come to any fruition, Chin Peng proposed a referendum to the ruling British government alongside many Malayan officials in 1955.

Baling Talks.fact: The meeting was intended to pursue a mutual end to the conflict but the Malayan government representatives, led by Tunku Abdul Rahman, dismissed all of Chin Peng's demands.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: As a result, the conflict heightened and, in response, _____ sent NZSAS soldiers, No
Baling Talks.fact: As a result, the conflict heightened and, in response, New Zealand sent NZSAS soldiers, No.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society

Baling Talks.fact: 14 Squadron RNZAF and later No. 75 Squadron RNZAF; and other Commonwealth members also sent troops to aid the British.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: 75 _____ RNZAF; and other Commonwealth members also sent troops to aid the British
Baling Talks.fact: 14 Squadron RNZAF and later No. 75 Squadron RNZAF; and other Commonwealth members also sent troops to aid the British.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: However, for as long as the _____ threat persisted, the Tunku believed that the British government would not grant self-government to Malaya
Baling Talks.fact: However, for as long as the Communist threat persisted, the Tunku believed that the British government would not grant self-government to Malaya. The Tunku's interpretation was based on the British Government directive to Sir Gerald Templer, on his appointment as the new High Commissioner for Malaya in 1951, which stated that "Her Majesty's Government would not lay aside the responsibility in Malaya until they are satisfied that Communist Terrorism has been defeated".

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The termination of the _____ was the first priority of the Alliance, and it had to attempt every means possible to achieve it
Baling Talks.fact: The termination of the Emergency was the first priority of the Alliance, and it had to attempt every means possible to achieve it. It was to this end that, in early January 1955, the Tunku made a dramatic call for the granting of an amnesty to the Communists as part of a deal to bring to an end the state of emergency in Malaya.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: It was to this end that, in early January _____, the Tunku made a dramatic call for the granting of an amnesty to the Communists as part of a deal to bring to an end the state of emergency in Malaya
Baling Talks.fact: It was to this end that, in early January 1955, the Tunku made a dramatic call for the granting of an amnesty to the Communists as part of a deal to bring to an end the state of emergency in Malaya.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: His proposal contemplated the granting of amnesty and the intensification of the campaign against the _____ if the amnesty was rejected
Baling Talks.fact: It was to this end that, in early January 1955, the Tunku made a dramatic call for the granting of an amnesty to the Communists as part of a deal to bring to an end the state of emergency in Malaya. The Tunku's proposal envisaged that, since a more truly national form of government was about to be introduced into the Federation, the Communists could no longer assert that they were fighting against British Imperialism and would be ready to give up the struggle.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: Dato' _____, then-President of the Malayan Chinese Association (MCA) echoed the Tunku's sentiment, and even went so far as to publicly volunteer to go into the jungle to negotiate with the Communists
Baling Talks.fact: Dato' Seri Tan Cheng Lock, then-President of the Malayan Chinese Association (MCA) echoed the Tunku's sentiment, and even went so far as to publicly volunteer to go into the jungle to negotiate with the Communists.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: On 12 January _____, a meeting of the UMNO-MCA Alliance was held in Malacca to discuss the Tunku's amnesty proposal
Baling Talks.fact: On 12 January 1955, a meeting of the UMNO-MCA Alliance was held in Malacca to discuss the Tunku's amnesty proposal.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The meeting decided to "ask the _____ to offer amnesty terms to the Communist terrorists"
Baling Talks.fact: The meeting decided to "ask the Federation Government to offer amnesty terms to the Communist terrorists".

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The Committee decision was that "terrorists accepting the amnesty should be sent back to People's _____ of China or be rehabilitated and allowed to remain good citizens"
Baling Talks.fact: The Committee decision was that "terrorists accepting the amnesty should be sent back to People's Republic of China or be rehabilitated and allowed to remain good citizens".

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: There was a fear that the ending of the amnesty period would discourage further surrenders, until confidence was again built up in the treatment of surrendered _____ under normal conditions
Baling Talks.fact: The British did not believe that, under the circumstances in January 1955, the offer of an amnesty would be likely to entice the Communists to surrender en-bloc, than their current policy of encouraging the terrorists to surrender individually, in the understanding that they would be fairly and humanely treated. There was a fear that the ending of the amnesty period would discourage further surrenders, until confidence was again built up in the treatment of surrendered Communists under normal...

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: On 11 January _____, Tunku Abdul Rahman met the Director of Operations, Lt
Baling Talks.fact: On 11 January 1955, Tunku Abdul Rahman met the Director of Operations, Lt.

Baling Talks.question: On 11 January 1955, _____ met the Director of Operations, Lt
Baling Talks.fact: On 11 January 1955, Tunku Abdul Rahman met the Director of Operations, Lt.

Baling Talks.fact: The Tunku stated that his objective was not so much that the MCP would accept an offer of amnesty, but to convince the people of Malaya that everything possible was being done.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: He was aware that any direct negotiation with the _____ was out of the question
Baling Talks.fact: He was aware that any direct negotiation with the Communists was out of the question. He stressed that it would not be acceptable for the Communists Party to be allowed to operate legally.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: He stressed that it would not be acceptable for the _____ to be allowed to operate legally
Baling Talks.fact: He stressed that it would not be acceptable for the Communists Party to be allowed to operate legally.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The proposal was further discussed on 17 January by the Director of _____, which comprised not only the Director of Operations and his Service Advisers, but a number of political leaders
Baling Talks.fact: The proposal was further discussed on 17 January by the Director of Operations Committee, which comprised not only the Director of Operations and his Service Advisers, but a number of political leaders.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The Alliance was represented by _____ and H.S. Lee
Baling Talks.fact: The Alliance was represented by Tunku Abdul Rahman and H.S. Lee.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The Tunku was asked by the _____ to clarify his amnesty proposal and the eight-point arrangements for an amnesty as proposed by the UMNO-MCA Alliance meeting at Malacca
Baling Talks.fact: The proposal was further discussed on 17 January by the Director of Operations Committee, which comprised not only the Director of Operations and his Service Advisers, but a number of political leaders. The Tunku was asked by the Committee to clarify his amnesty proposal and the eight-point arrangements for an amnesty as proposed by the UMNO-MCA Alliance meeting at Malacca.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: Further publicity about the amnesty was also considered to be undesirable as it would adversely affect conduct of the campaign to encourage the _____ to surrender to the Government
Baling Talks.fact: After the discussion, it was appreciated by the Tunku and H.S. Lee that an amnesty will not be an armistice - something to be negotiated separately with the Communists' leaders - but will be a standing offer of pardon for each individual terrorist. Further publicity about the amnesty was also considered to be undesirable as it would adversely affect conduct of the campaign to encourage the Communists to surrender to the Government.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The findings were to be recorded for the information of the Director of _____
Baling Talks.fact: The findings were to be recorded for the information of the Director of Operations Committee. After the meeting, the following press release was issued: The question of an amnesty was very fully discussed in every respect at the Director of Operations Committee today.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: After the meeting, the following press release was issued: The question of an amnesty was very fully discussed in every respect at the Director of _____ today
Baling Talks.fact: The findings were to be recorded for the information of the Director of Operations Committee. After the meeting, the following press release was issued: The question of an amnesty was very fully discussed in every respect at the Director of Operations Committee today.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: Realizing that his struggles had not come to any fruition, _____ proposed a referendum to the ruling British government alongside many Malayan officials in 1955
Baling Talks.fact: Realizing that his struggles had not come to any fruition, Chin Peng proposed a referendum to the ruling British government alongside many Malayan officials in 1955. Baling Talks.fact: The rejection by the Federal Government of the Alliance's proposal for an amnesty was strongly supported by the Manchester Guardian, a British newspaper.

Baling Talks.question: However, this was not the case in _____
Baling Talks.fact: However, this was not the case in Malaya.

Baling Talks.fact: The rejection by the Federal Government of the Alliance's proposal for an amnesty was strongly supported by the Manchester Guardian, a British newspaper. In its editorial, the newspaper commented that an amnesty was appropriate when rebels had lost the desire to continue the struggle with the Government, and in return for the act of oblivion, were willing to become law-abiding citizens again.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The Tunku however was not prepared to give way lightly to the shelving of his proposals and the Alliance restated its view on the question of an amnesty in its Election Manifesto issues in May _____
Baling Talks.fact: The Tunku however was not prepared to give way lightly to the shelving of his proposals and the Alliance restated its view on the question of an amnesty in its Election Manifesto issues in May 1955.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The Manifesto contained an undertaking to offer a general amnesty to the _____ in the following terms: ..
Baling Talks.fact: The form of amnesty which was proposed by the Alliance seemed to envisage that the Communists would maintain their party organisation intact and would turn their acts of guerrilla warfare to electioneering in a constitutional way. The Manifesto contained an undertaking to offer a general amnesty to the Communists in the following terms: ..

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The offer was contained in a letter written in _____, copies of which were sent to a number of leading personalities and organisations in the Federation of Malaya and in Singapore
Baling Talks.fact: The offer was contained in a letter written in Chinese, copies of which were sent to a number of leading personalities and organisations in the Federation of Malaya and in Singapore.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The letter was signed by a representative of the _____ and dated 1 May, and had been posted in Haadyai in Southern Thailand
Baling Talks.fact: The letter was signed by a representative of the Malayan National Liberation Army and dated 1 May, and had been posted in Haadyai in Southern Thailand.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: None of these letters were sent direct to the _____ or to any of his officers
Baling Talks.fact: None of these letters were sent direct to the High Commissioner or to any of his officers.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The letter also rejected the _____'s amnesty offer
Baling Talks.fact: The letter also rejected the Alliance's amnesty offer.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: Furthermore, the offer was consistent with the then _____ policy of turning away from armed struggle to expansion by political means
Baling Talks.fact: Furthermore, the offer was consistent with the then International Communist policy of turning away from armed struggle to expansion by political means.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society

Baling Talks.fact: At the second Conference of the Communist and Workers' Parties of the British Commonwealth, held in London in April 1954, a report entitled Malaya Fights for Freedom had been submitted by the exiled Lim Hong Bee that favoured, among other things, a provisional coalition People's government formed by all patriotic parties to achieve full national independence. In August 1954 a Malayan delegate to the Council of World Democratic Youth in Peking was quoted as saying "..

Baling Talks.fact: At the second Conference of the Communist and Workers' Parties of the British Commonwealth, held in London in April 1954, a report entitled Malaya Fights for Freedom had been submitted by the exiled Lim Hong Bee that favoured, among other things, a provisional coalition People's government formed by all patriotic parties to achieve full national independence. In August 1954 a Malayan delegate to the Council of World Democratic Youth in Peking was quoted as saying "..

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society

Baling Talks.fact: The MCP's counter-proposal was discussed both by the Executive Council and the Director of Operations Committee.

Baling Talks.question: At this meeting, which was attended by _____ and other leaders, a unanimous decision was made to reject the MCP's proposal
Baling Talks.fact: At this meeting, which was attended by Tunku Abdul Rahman and other leaders, a unanimous decision was made to reject the MCP's proposal.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The Government believed that the terrorist leaders in _____ had their own considerations to call off the war
Baling Talks.fact: The Government believed that the terrorist leaders in Malaya had their own considerations to call off the war.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: It was thought that MCP leaders realised that they were slowly and steadily losing ground to the _____ and wished to concentrate their main efforts on subversion
Baling Talks.fact: It was thought that MCP leaders realised that they were slowly and steadily losing ground to the Security Forces and wished to concentrate their main efforts on subversion.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: Reactions to this refusal by the _____ were varied
Baling Talks.fact: Reactions to this refusal by the Government were varied. Among the Chinese newspapers, only the Nanyang Siang Pau had questioned the wisdom of the Government's rejection.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The rejection was supported by the Alliance and _____
Baling Talks.fact: The rejection was supported by the Alliance and Parti Negara.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The Labour Party of _____, however, expressed the view that the rejection was in haste and that the offer should have been more further examined
Baling Talks.fact: The Labour Party of Malaya, however, expressed the view that the rejection was in haste and that the offer should have been more further examined.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: Among the _____ newspapers, only the Nanyang Siang Pau had questioned the wisdom of the Government's rejection
Baling Talks.fact: Among the Chinese newspapers, only the Nanyang Siang Pau had questioned the wisdom of the Government's rejection. The other Chinese newspapers, particularly those with a KMT or Chinese Nationalist background, strongly supported the Government's rejection and described the peace offer as a manoeuvre to bring about the relaxation of military pressure which would facilitate the infiltration.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: This paper argued that the offer was worthy of closer attention than it had received and that nothing would have been lost by meeting the _____ at the table to test their sincerity
Baling Talks.fact: This paper argued that the offer was worthy of closer attention than it had received and that nothing would have been lost by meeting the Communists at the table to test their sincerity. The Committee, which discussed the matter at a series of meetings held in June and July, decided to offer an amnesty to the Communists.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The Committee, which discussed the matter at a series of meetings held in June and July, decided to offer an amnesty to the _____
Baling Talks.fact: This paper argued that the offer was worthy of closer attention than it had received and that nothing would have been lost by meeting the Communists at the table to test their sincerity. The Committee, which discussed the matter at a series of meetings held in June and July, decided to offer an amnesty to the Communists.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The Committee also took into consideration the declaration made by the Alliance in their _____ that, if they were successful at the Elections, they would declare an amnesty
Baling Talks.fact: The Committee also took into consideration the declaration made by the Alliance in their Election Manifesto that, if they were successful at the Elections, they would declare an amnesty.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: Since the expectations were that the _____ would be the major party, it was clearly prudent that some thoughts should be given in advance to the ways to which an amnesty offer might be made
Baling Talks.fact: The Committee also took into consideration the declaration made by the Alliance in their Election Manifesto that, if they were successful at the Elections, they would declare an amnesty. Since the expectations were that the Alliance would be the major party, it was clearly prudent that some thoughts should be given in advance to the ways to which an amnesty offer might be made.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: If the _____ opposed the granting of an amnesty it would play into the hands of the Communists for propaganda purposes
Baling Talks.fact: If the Government opposed the granting of an amnesty it would play into the hands of the Communists for propaganda purposes. The Director of Operations Committee concluded, however, that the advantages of offering an amnesty outweighed the possible risks and difficulties, and that the offer would carry particular weight if it were made by the new Government soon after the elections.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The only objection to granting an amnesty, according to the _____, was that it would have a deadline
Baling Talks.fact: The Committee also took into consideration the declaration made by the Alliance in their Election Manifesto that, if they were successful at the Elections, they would declare an amnesty. The only objection to granting an amnesty, according to the Committee, was that it would have a deadline.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: To this end, the _____ began to draft the wording of the amnesty terms
Baling Talks.fact: The only objection to granting an amnesty, according to the Committee, was that it would have a deadline. The Director of Operations Committee concluded, however, that the advantages of offering an amnesty outweighed the possible risks and difficulties, and that the offer would carry particular weight if it were made by the new Government soon after the elections.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: Though those who surrender would not be prosecuted, they would be required to demonstrate their loyalty to the _____ before they would be allowed to return to their families
Baling Talks.fact: The Director of Operations Committee concluded, however, that the advantages of offering an amnesty outweighed the possible risks and difficulties, and that the offer would carry particular weight if it were made by the new Government soon after the elections. Though those who surrender would not be prosecuted, they would be required to demonstrate their loyalty to the Government before they would be allowed to return to their families.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The amnesty involved neither negotiation with the _____ nor recognition of the MCP
Baling Talks.fact: Malcolm MacDonald, the British Commissioner-General for Southeast Asia, suggested that the terms should be designed to appeal to the rank-and-file terrorists who, not being hardcore Communists, had been intimidated by the Communists into taking up arms and having done so, had been forced to stay in the jungle. The amnesty involved neither negotiation with the Communists nor recognition of the MCP.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The British Ministry of _____ was also involved in drafting the terms
Baling Talks.fact: The British Ministry of Defence was also involved in drafting the terms.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The Ministry considered that the point to be stressed was that _____ who surrendered would not be shot, but that no hope should be held out that they would escape detention
Baling Talks.fact: The amnesty involved neither negotiation with the Communists nor recognition of the MCP. The Ministry considered that the point to be stressed was that Communists who surrendered would not be shot, but that no hope should be held out that they would escape detention.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The Ministry thought that the amnesty terms should not include any reference to the possibility of helping a _____ who surrendered to leave the country
Baling Talks.fact: The Ministry considered that the point to be stressed was that Communists who surrendered would not be shot, but that no hope should be held out that they would escape detention. Furthermore, it added that, it was essential that hard core Communists should be detained for some time, as it was believed if they were released into society, they would cause further trouble in Malaya and if they were deported, they would cause trouble in Southeast Asia.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The MCP was represented by _____, the Secretary-General, Rashid Maidin and Chen Tien, head of the MCP's Central Propaganda Department
Baling Talks.fact: The MCP was represented by Chin Peng, the Secretary-General, Rashid Maidin and Chen Tien, head of the MCP's Central Propaganda Department.

In his opening remarks, Tunku Abdul Rahman thanked the Communists for the confidence they had shown in coming to the meeting.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The British Government intended to enter the London talks in _____ "on that understanding"
Baling Talks.fact: The British Government intended to enter the London talks in January "on that understanding".

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society

Baling Talks.fact: Since then the UMNO Assembly had passed a very important resolution to the effect that independence for Malaya must be given by 31 August 1957.

Baling Talks.question: The Tunku then explained to _____ that the objective of his Party was to bring peace to the country
Baling Talks.fact: The Tunku then explained to Chin Peng that the objective of his Party was to bring peace to the country.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: The Tunku reiterated that if the _____ accepted the amnesty "everyone would be pardoned." The Tunku then explained the amnesty terms in full
Baling Talks.fact: But, in his opinion, there would be no way of bringing about peace other than to offer suitable amnesty terms for the surrender of the Communists. The Tunku reiterated that if the Communists accepted the amnesty "everyone would be pardoned." The Tunku then explained the amnesty terms in full.

Baling Talks.question: He added that the _____ had carried out its part of the terms with regard to local ceasefires but that the Communists had continued offensive action

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: As a result, ceasefire arrangements had been suspended by the Government, although the _____ would like to know the reason
Baling Talks.fact: As a result, ceasefire arrangements had been suspended by the Government, although the Security Forces would like to know the reason.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society

Baling Talks.fact: First, however, the communists would have to show their loyalty to Malaysia.

Baling Talks.subject: Women & Society
Baling Talks.question: In his view, simply to be anti-_____ was not sufficient to show that one was loyal to Malaya
Baling Talks.fact: In his view, simply to be anti-British was not sufficient to show that one was loyal to Malaya.

Baling Talks.question: The Tunku pointed out that the _____ people regarded the Communist activities as something entirely foreign to the Malayan way of life
Baling Talks.fact: The Tunku pointed out that the Malayan people regarded the Communist activities as something entirely foreign to the Malayan way of life. During the second session, the discussion revolved around the question of loyalty to Malaya and recognition of the Malayan Communist Party.

Baling Talks.fact: They regarded the Communist Party as belonging to a power outside the country and considered that its members gave allegiance to that foreign country and not Malaya. During the second session, the discussion revolved around the question of loyalty to Malaya and recognition of the Malayan Communist Party.
